To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
open science practices are essential for computational communication science and that individual scholars should adopt them as a matter of course.

the reusability and reproducibility of data and code can be improved through the use of open science practices, such as the creation of reusable workflows, the recognition of tools and code as academic work, and the use of open-source software.
open science practices can be applied to computational communication science and that this can lead to more reusable data and code.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to create and maintain a community that values reusability of computational communication science.
the practical implementation of the reusability principles and practices of open science in the context of CCS.
making data and code reusable and accessible, and with making research more reproducible, transparent, and efficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reusability and reproducibility of data and code are not only desirable, but also essential to advance computational communication science and the field of communication research more broadly.
open computational communication science is the future of the field.
we are at the dawn of an exciting new era of computational communication science.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
open science is a means to an end, and the end is reproducible science.
open computational communication science is not only possible but also highly desirable.
we are not arguing that researchers need to do more, but rather that they should do what they are already doing, but in a more structured and organized way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reusability goals can be achieved through the integration of the research and data management process into the research workflow, which can be supported by the development of a community of practice.
the reusability and openness of data and code are not just a matter of good scientific practice but also a matter of scientific progress.
the reusability agenda is not a burden for individual researchers but a necessary and important step for the field to advance.
